text:
Mason McTavish has two points in his last ten games for St. Louis. That is the bad news. The good news is almost everything underneath it.

The former third overall pick has 53 shots in 20 games and 8.22 expected goals (the quality of his chances), the kind of volume that usually ends in goals. He has seven, slightly under what his chances deserve, and the Blues have scored 3.2 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice, which is costing him assists too. Over those last ten he generated 3.4 expected goals and scored once. That is a drought built on bad luck, not bad play.

His first season in St. Louis has him at 16 minutes a night and holding his own at five on five, a touch better than the team without him. The old question from Anaheim still applies: Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level last season, driving offense in the 86th percentile but giving up chances in the bottom 2% of forwards. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a setup man, 7.9 primary shot assists per 60. Keep an eye on the defensive side; the scoring should sort itself out.
headline: McTavish is shooting into a wall
